questions.stem: This curve plots developed tension/stroke volume against preload (end-diastolic volume or pressure). What physiologic principle does it depict?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The exponential rise of diastolic pressure with filling volume

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Frank-Starling relationship

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pressure-volume loop area representing stroke work

choices.label: D
choices.text: Afterload mismatch causing progressive fall in stroke volume

choices.label: E
choices.text: Autoregulation of coronary blood flow with perfusion pressure

explanation.summary: The rising, then plateauing, curve of force versus preload is the Frank-Starling mechanism: greater end-diastolic stretch increases actin-myosin overlap and contractile force until overstretch limits further gain.
explanation.whyCorrect: The rising, then plateauing, curve of force versus preload is the Frank-Starling mechanism: greater end-diastolic stretch increases actin-myosin overlap and contractile force until overstretch limits further gain.

questions.stem: These left ventricular pressure-volume loops show three beats with equal preload but progressively higher afterload (1 < 2 < 3). What happens to stroke volume as afterload rises?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stroke volume decreases because the ventricle ejects against greater resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stroke volume increases as the aortic valve opens at a higher pressure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stroke volume is unchanged because preload is held constant

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contractility increases to fully compensate, keeping ejection fraction constant

choices.label: E
choices.text: End-diastolic volume falls with each successive beat

explanation.summary: With preload fixed, raising afterload forces the ventricle to reach a higher pressure before the aortic valve opens, so it ejects a smaller volume; end-systolic volume rises and stroke volume falls.
explanation.whyCorrect: With preload fixed, raising afterload forces the ventricle to reach a higher pressure before the aortic valve opens, so it ejects a smaller volume; end-systolic volume rises and stroke volume falls.

questions.stem: According to the relationships summarized in this schematic, which single change would be expected to DECREASE stroke volume?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An increase in ventricular compliance to stretch

choices.label: B
choices.text: An increase in total blood volume

choices.label: C
choices.text: An increase in myocardial contractility from sympathetic input

choices.label: D
choices.text: An increase in systemic vascular resistance

choices.label: E
choices.text: An increase in venous return raising central venous pressure

explanation.summary: Increased SVR raises afterload, which opposes ejection and lowers stroke volume; increased preload, contractility, compliance, and blood volume all tend to raise stroke volume.
explanation.whyCorrect: Increased SVR raises afterload, which opposes ejection and lowers stroke volume; increased preload, contractility, compliance, and blood volume all tend to raise stroke volume.

questions.stem: In this schematic of blood flowing from veins through the heart to arteries, the load the ventricle must overcome to push blood out into the arteries corresponds to which parameter?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Heart rate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contractility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Afterload

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preload

choices.label: E
choices.text: Compliance

explanation.summary: Afterload is the force/resistance the ventricle works against during ejection, represented by the arterial (downstream) side; preload reflects venous filling, while contractility and heart rate are intrinsic cardiac properties.
explanation.whyCorrect: Afterload is the force/resistance the ventricle works against during ejection, represented by the arterial (downstream) side; preload reflects venous filling, while contractility and heart rate are intrinsic cardiac properties.

questions.topicName: Cardiac - Compliance, Contractility, Preload, and Afterload
questions.stem: On these LV diastolic pressure-volume curves, the rightward-shifted red curve reaches a given end-diastolic volume at a lower pressure. What does this curve represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduced preload from hypovolemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated afterload opposing ejection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased compliance from a stiff, hypertrophied ventricle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased contractility during systole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased ventricular compliance

explanation.summary: Compliance is the change in volume per change in pressure; a curve shifted right/down accommodates more volume at lower filling pressure, indicating increased compliance, whereas a steep left-shifted curve (higher EDP for the same EDV) indicates a stiff, less compliant ventricle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Compliance is the change in volume per change in pressure; a curve shifted right/down accommodates more volume at lower filling pressure, indicating increased compliance, whereas a steep left-shifted curve (higher EDP for the same EDV) indicates a stiff, less compliant ventricle.

questions.stem: These curves plot active tension against sarcomere length (preload). The upward shift of the red curve labeled with the arrow reflects a change in which property?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased ventricular compliance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased contractility (positive inotropy)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased afterload

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased preload at constant contractility

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased heart rate (chronotropy)

explanation.summary: Shifting the length-tension curve upward so that more tension is generated at any given sarcomere length reflects increased inotropy/contractility, independent of the preload (length) on the x-axis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Shifting the length-tension curve upward so that more tension is generated at any given sarcomere length reflects increased inotropy/contractility, independent of the preload (length) on the x-axis.

questions.topicName: Cardiac - Compliance, Contractility, Preload, and Afterload
questions.stem: The upper panel resolves muscle tension into two components at increasing lengths. Which relationship explains why total tension equals the sum shown?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Total tension equals passive tension minus active tension

choices.label: B
choices.text: Active tension arises only after passive tension plateaus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Total tension is independent of muscle length

choices.label: D
choices.text: Total tension is the sum of passive tension and active tension

choices.label: E
choices.text: Passive tension is generated by cross-bridge cycling

explanation.summary: Stretching muscle generates passive elastic tension; stimulation adds active cross-bridge tension. Their sum is the total tension, and active tension is derived by subtracting passive from total at each length.
explanation.whyCorrect: Stretching muscle generates passive elastic tension; stimulation adds active cross-bridge tension. Their sum is the total tension, and active tension is derived by subtracting passive from total at each length.
